ruled_out_vectors.title: Pool type return value manipulation bounded by reserve underflow
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Malicious pool type could inflate amountOut to drain reserves
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool type returns amountOut which Core trusts, BUT _safeDecrementUint128 at AMMModule.sol:1437/1440 reverts on underflow if amountOut exceeds reserve. Additionally, actualAmountIn is validated <= originalAmountIn at L1405-1406. Fees validated by _validateProtocolFees at L1431. Combined, a malicious pool type cannot extract more than the pool's actual reserves.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Reentrancy during hook fee execution via flag clearing
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) at AMMModule.sol:3190 clears custom flags during swap, allowing reentry through flag-gated paths
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The ENTERED bit (bit 1) survives _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) because the function preserves `currentGuard & ENTERED` (TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:70-71). All nonReentrant/nonReentrantWithFlags functions check ENTERED bit first. While collectHookFeesByHook (ModuleFeeCollection.sol:72-82) changes behavior (queue -> immediate transfer when SWAP_GUARD_FLAG is cleared), the tokensOwed accounting prevents double-spending: _transferHookFeesByHook deducts from tokensOwed before safeTransfer, so calling it again would try to deduct from 0 and revert/underflow.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Handler callback reentrancy after output disbursement
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Handler callback executes after output token sent, could re-enter AMM to manipulate state
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Handler callback at AMMModule.sol:2250-2252 executes after output disbursement (L2235-2244), hook fee execution (L2246-2248), and flag clearing (L3190). However: (1) ENTERED bit is preserved - all nonReentrant functions blocked, (2) callback memory is in caller's EVM frame, isolated from self-call frame, (3) handler address is fixed from initial call, (4) both concrete handlers (CLOBTransferHandler, PermitTransferHandler) verify msg.sender == AMM, (5) callback data is immutable in memory between handler execution and callback.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: Traced _executeTransferHandler (L2272-2321) and _executeTransferHandlerCallback (L2330-2341). CLOBTransferHandler.afterSwapRefund checks msg.sender == AMM at L316. PermitTransferHandler returns empty callback data (no callback executed).

ruled_out_vectors.title: DynamicPoolType namespace isolation bypass
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: DynamicPoolType lacks onlyAMM modifier, attacker could manipulate pools cross-namespace
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: DynamicPoolType uses globalState[msg.sender] for ALL state-mutating operations (createPool, swapByInput, swapByOutput, addLiquidity, removeLiquidity, collectFees). Each caller gets completely isolated storage. View functions accept an `address amm` parameter allowing cross-namespace reads but only for information disclosure - no state modification possible.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: Analyzed DynamicPoolType.sol: globalState mapping keyed by msg.sender at lines 71, 161, 228, 321, 444, 563. View functions (getCurrentPriceX96, getPoolState, getPositionInfo, getTickInfo) accept address parameter but are read-only.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Flash loan fee token denomination mismatch
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Flash loan fee computed in loan token denomination but charged in different token (MUX-style bug)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Flash loan has two intentional paths: (A) No hook: fee = loanAmount * flashLoanBPS / MAX_BPS, denominated in loanToken - same token. (B) Hook returns cross-token fee: fee = tokenFeeAmount + tokenFeeAmount * flashLoanBPS / MAX_BPS, ALL computed in feeToken units. Balance checks are split correctly: same-token path checks one balance (L3310-3311), cross-token path checks BOTH loanToken and feeToken balances independently (L3312-3314, L3348-3370).
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: Traced _flashLoan (AMMModule.sol:3288-3382) and _executeTokenFlashloanHooks (L3404-3437). Both fee paths maintain correct denomination throughout.

ruled_out_vectors.title: MultiSwap intermediate hop validation gap
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Intermediate hops in multiSwap receive weaker validation than first/last hop
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Each hop executes identical validation: (1) Token chain continuity enforced via pool token matching + nextToken propagation (L1356-1370), (2) Same hook execution (before+after) with per-hop hook data, (3) Same pool fee calculation via _getPoolFee, (4) Same reserve update via _safeIncrement/DecrementUint128, (5) Per-hop protocol fee storage for multi-hop at L1455.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: Traced _poolSwapByInput loop (LimitBreakAMM.sol:312-316, AMMModule.sol:1343-1470). 11 invariants verified. No asymmetry between intermediate and terminal hops except intentional partial fill restriction.

ruled_out_vectors.title: directSwap vs singleSwap validation asymmetry exploitation
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: directSwap bypasses pool-level validation, enabling price manipulation or fee bypass
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Comprehensive Lens 2 diff reveals directSwap is architecturally different (P2P, no pool state) but has equivalent safety guarantees: (1) Same _initializeSwapCache for exchange fee/feeOnTop validation, (2) Same _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse for balance verification, (3) Hook fees still applied (poolFeeBPS=0 but hopFeeBPS from token settings still enforced), (4) AMMStandardHook has direct-swap specific pricing bounds via two-phase transient storage, (5) _collectToken at L2913-2920 has identical balance verification to L2206-2213.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: Full L2 diff: 11 checks in singleSwap but not directSwap (all pool-specific, N/A for P2P), 9 checks in directSwap but not singleSwap (all P2P-specific).

ruled_out_vectors.title: Diamond storage collision between modules
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Multiple modules using delegatecall could have storage slot collisions at the diamond storage slot
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All modules use diamond storage pattern at slot 0x9A1D via LBAMMStorage.sol. No module declares direct storage variables (0 slots in storage layout). The diamond storage struct is shared across all modules by design. Transient storage slots use distinct constants from Constants.sol.
ruled_out_vectors.evidence: test_C15_noStorageCollisions_diamondPattern (PASS). Verified via Slither storage layout analysis.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Hook fee overflow/underflow during fee application
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: Hook returning extreme fee values could overflow/underflow swap amount calculations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee application functions have explicit bounds: _applySwapByInputInputFees at L2616 checks totalFees <= swapAmountIn and reverts with LBAMM__HookFeeExceedsSwapAmount. _applySwapByInputOutputFees at L2711 checks hookOutputFees <= adjustedAmountOut. Combined hook fees are bounded by the swap amount they're derived from.

ruled_out_vectors.title: Transient storage cross-path contamination in direct swap pricing
ruled_out_vectors.hypothesis: DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT written by one direct swap could be read by another in same transaction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The SWAP_GUARD_FLAG (bit 2) is set by both singleSwap and directSwap via their respective guard flags. This prevents any concurrent swap from the same entry point within the same transaction. The transient storage slot (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) is only read during afterSwap pricing validation, which occurs in the same swap as the beforeSwap that wrote it.

hypothesis_results.detail: Pool type return values are bounded by _safeDecrementUint128 (reserve underflow), actualAmountIn <= original check, and _validateProtocolFees. No extraction beyond pool reserves possible.
ENTERED bit (bit 1) survives _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) at L3190. Custom flag clearing changes collectHookFeesByHook behavior but tokensOwed accounting prevents double-spending.
Handler callback blocked by ENTERED bit. Both CLOBTransferHandler and PermitTransferHandler verify msg.sender == AMM. Callback data immutable in caller's memory frame.
DynamicPoolType namespace isolation via globalState[msg.sender] is complete. All 6 state-mutating functions use msg.sender key. Cross-namespace views are read-only.
Flash loan fee denomination is correct in both paths. Same-token: fee in loanToken. Cross-token: fee in feeToken with separate balance checks. No MUX-style mismatch.
MultiSwap hops validated identically. Token chain continuity via nextToken propagation. Partial fills restricted to hop 0. Fees per-hop with correct token attribution.
directSwap has equivalent safety to singleSwap despite being pool-less. Same balance verification, hook fee enforcement, and slippage protection. Two-phase pricing bounds specific to direct swaps.
Diamond storage at 0x9A1D shared by design. No module has direct storage slots. No collision risk.

thesis.summary: The Limit Break AMM cross-boundary trust model is well-hardened across all 6 critical boundaries. Return values from pool types, handlers, and hooks are validated or bounded by the core module. The reentrancy guard preserves the ENTERED bit across flag operations, preventing re-entry. Denomination consistency is maintained in all fee paths including cross-token flash loan fees. The namespace isolation in DynamicPoolType and the directSwap validation path are architecturally sound.
thesis.strongest_defense: The combination of (1) strict balance verification (balanceBefore + amount != balanceAfter) on ALL token collections, (2) reserve-based output bounding via _safeDecrementUint128, and (3) the ENTERED bit surviving _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) creates a robust defense-in-depth that makes cross-boundary exploitation extremely difficult.
thesis.weakest_boundary: Core->Hook boundary has the most complexity: hooks can specify fees, block swaps, modify pricing bounds, and are called via assembly-optimized external calls. The flag clearing at L3190 changes collectHookFeesByHook behavior mid-swap. While not exploitable due to tokensOwed accounting, this is the boundary most likely to have a subtle bug in a future code change.
thesis.residual_risk: Two areas warrant ongoing attention: (1) Custom hook implementations beyond AMMStandardHook could introduce new cross-boundary risks not covered by the standard hook's defenses, (2) The two-phase direct swap pricing (beforeSwap stores, afterSwap validates) requires both hooks to be enabled for enforcement - misconfiguration could leave direct swaps without pricing bounds.
